messages:
Deploy Bot: FYI  new Dedicated pool 'sienna-sjc1' is live in SJC1 (San Jose). Pool flavor: Sienna-S (SLO-backed, low-jitter). Initial capacity: 28 instances. Tags: #dedicated #sienna #sjc1 :evergreen_tree:
Sahana R: TL;DR on Sienna? how is it different from Tempest/Polaris/Zephyr?
Tom B: Sienna is our SLO-focused SKU. Tuned for conversational workloads that need tight tail-latency SLOs (p99 SLOs). Hardware + runtime changes: aggressive KV prefetching, prioritized worker lanes, and micro-batching heuristics to reduce jitter. Expect p99 improvement of ~15-30% for chat workloads compared to standard pools.
Product Ops: policy change note: Sienna pools introduce a new "SLO Commit" reservation type. Teams can buy SLO Commit (monthly/annual) which guarantees allocation and non-preemptibility plus a latency SLA. Pricing and SLA details in the docs.
Billing Bot: billing update: new SKU 'dedicated.sienna' + new commitment type 'slo-commit' active now. Metering: per-instance-hour for slo-commit, per-instance-minute for burst. Intro offer: teams that sign any SLO Commit in the first 90 days get a migration rebate tiered at 3/6/9% depending on commit length (30/90/365d). Tag your reservation `slo-early` to auto-qualify.
Sahana R: important for platform teams: SLO Commit requires on-call contact and an SLO runbook uploaded to the Console. Product Ops, can you confirm requirements?
Product Ops: yes  onboarding checklist: 1) reserve SLO Commit in Console/CLI; 2) add `oncall=` tag with contact; 3) upload runbook link in Console; 4) enable perf-trace forwarding to the Console. We'll block SLO Commit if reqs missing. Docs: https://intra.redwood.dev/dedicated/sienna-sjc1/onboarding (internal).
Tom B: routing/fallback: default is strict-sienna (prefer Sienna for routes with sla:high). Fallback chain: sienna-sjc1-compat -> sjc1-standard -> global-h100. Note: if you purchase SLO Commit and enable "strict-slo-routing", your routes won't failover automatically; failover will require manual opt-in.
Sahana R: does Sienna support large KV caches? any model_profile changes?
Tom B: two model_profile options: sienna-default and sienna-kv-pro (for >24GB KV per worker). Quantization: supported 8-bit and dynamic 4-bit. No runtime ABI changes. If you see quality deviation, file an eval and tag Optimize + reference sienna-sjc1.
Security Bot: security note  SLO Commit customers can opt into Private Peering for Dedicated (VPC-to-VPC) in SJC1. That requires an approved compliance ticket and KMS binding. Contact security-oncall to start.
Infra Oncall: ops note: Sienna burst instances will be soft-preemptible during scheduled data-center maintenance windows. SLO Commit instances are non-preemptible and have prioritized warmup windows to avoid cold cache effects. We'll publish maintenance calendar in #infra-maintenance later today.
Sahana R: CLI/Example to reserve a 90d SLO Commit (example):
```
redwood reserve --pool sienna-sjc1 --count 4 --duration 90d --commit slo-commit --tags team=chat oncall=chat-oncall slo-early
```
Tom B: monitoring/observability: SLO Commit routes will automatically get a per-route latency SLO dashboard and a daily SLA digest emailed to the oncall contact. Enable "trace-sampling=high" in Console for full traces.
Product Ops: ops guidance: if you move traffic to Sienna and see >10% error increase or >15% p99 regression, tag @Infra Oncall and @Product Ops. For non-SLO commits, thresholds are slightly higher (15% error / 25% p99).
Billing Bot: operational tip: always set `team=` tag so costs and rebates appear in team dashboards. SLO rebates are applied automatically if the reservation includes `slo-early` and runbook/oncall info is present.
Infra Oncall: rollout timeline: day 0 (soft-open this announce), day 3 expand burst to 56 instances if health is green, day 14 enable SLO Commit annual option and add peering sign-up flows in Console.
Sahana R: any caveats around batching or throughput?
Tom B: batching heuristics are tuned for latency; recommend smaller batch sizes for SLO routes. If you need throughput, use a multi-route strategy: reserve SLO for latency-critical endpoints and normal pools for background heavy-batch workloads. We'll publish tuning notes in the doc.
Product Ops: docs: https://intra.redwood.dev/dedicated/sienna-sjc1 (internal). Pool ID: sienna-sjc1-101. API note: model_profile sienna-default / sienna-kv-pro.
Sahana R: thanks everyone. We'll run canaries later today and post p50/p95/p99 numbers. :thumbsup:
Infra Oncall: health checks are running; expect brief warmup spikes in agent metrics, not user-facing. Escalate if you see sustained >5% error or >20% p99 delta. :mag:
